## Summary

Appreciation tweet: the **Deflated Sharpe Ratio** is "simply genius" — unusually, an academic paper Martin implemented in practice **without having to make adjustments** for limitations or shortcomings. "It's good out of the box." He's been looking into it (truncated at capture).

The graphic (reconstructed by OCR) explains DSR in three steps:

1. **How far the best of many lands, from the number of tries.** With many no-edge strategies spread by luck around 0, the highest result lands a predictable number of standard deviations above 0 — growing slowly with N: 10 tries → ~1.6σ, 100 → ~2.5σ, 1,170 → ~3.3σ. Example: luck level 2.0 = 3.3 × 0.6 spread — what the best of 1,170 strategies with *no edge* would typically reach.
2. **"What if the best is just lucky?"** That is exactly what the luck level encodes. If the best is only luck, its Sharpe lands ≈ the luck level and **DSR comes out around 0.5 or below**; only a best *above* the luck level earns a high DSR. Trying more strategies gives more chances at a luckier best but raises the luck level by the same logic — the two cancel out.
3. **Why look only at the best?** Because expecting the best to be the luckiest *is the assumption DSR tests*: whether the best beat what the luckiest pure-luck strategy would reach. Worked example: a measured Sharpe of **1.70 gives DSR 0.19** against a 2.0 benchmark — i.e. only a 19% chance the true Sharpe exceeds 2.0, because a Sharpe measured over a few years carries estimation error; 95% confidence would require a measured Sharpe near **2.7**.

## Why it matters

- **The statistical formalization of the vault's verification bar.** [[2026-08-29-milk-man-replication-metrics]] scrutinizes claimed Sharpes; DSR is the tool that *prices in the number of strategies tried* before believing any single best one. The claimed-1.87-Sharpe case in [[2026-09-09-l1vsun-yield-curve-aware-momentum]] (zero replication path, unknown trial count) is exactly what a DSR screen exists to deflate.
- **The ex-post half of the same author's ex-ante rule.** [[2026-10-01-dmartin-hypothesis-first]] limits N up front (no mechanism, no build); DSR deflates whatever selection remains after the fact. Two halves of one epistemics: reduce trials ex ante, pay the trial-count tax ex post.
- **Explains IS→OOS decay as arithmetic, not bad luck.** The disclosure bar in [[2026-09-04-systematicpeter-why-publish-research]] treats in-sample→out-of-sample Sharpe decay as the honest tell; DSR shows *why* the best-of-N backtest decays — the luck level rises with N even as each new try looks "better".
- **Skepticism gates:** the OCR tail is partially garbled (rows 2–3 of the "why look only at the best" section); the σ-table, the 0.5 threshold logic, and the 1.70→0.19 / 2.7 worked example are clean. The graphic deliberately omits the full DSR machinery (variance, skew, kurtosis, N adjustments per Bailey & López de Prado) — "good out of the box" is Martin's practitioner verdict, not a claim the formula is trivial.
